societies.name: Lancer — Union’s Third Committee Core
societies.society: Implemented Metropolitan necessities guarantees supported by printing

scope.period: The functioning Galactic Core during established Third Committee government
scope.population: Living human Metropolitan residents in Core settlements implementing the Pillars
exclusions: Every member nation or remote Diasporan world
Harrison Armory and the Baronies as identical to Core society
Union’s aspirations as proof of implementation everywhere

societies.description:
Union’s developed Core combines printing and large-scale technological production with a material floor covering food, water and shelter. The Utopian Pillars make that floor a right, and the reference distinguishes their strong Metropolitan implementation from the unfinished project across the Diaspora. Guarantees therefore lie near the secure end for this selected Core population. The point does not turn every world nominally aligned with Union into an accomplished utopia.

Union is described as communal and post-capital, but the short references do not establish ordinary humans’ final ownership and override powers across the whole Core. Control remains unresolved, with a shared-human regime as the provisional classification rather than an automatic numeric conclusion from government rhetoric. Printing systems and nonhuman assistants do not themselves establish AI sovereignty. Residents still undertake research, administration, art, care, service and useful production. Freedom from survival wages, and the right to just labor, do not establish how many people undertake none of those activities. The nonworking fraction remains unknown.

guarantees.basis: The material Pillar, strong Metropolitan implementation and explicit printing/mass-production support establish the scoped floor; uneven Diaspora enforcement is excluded.

control.basis: Communal/post-capital institutions suggest a shared-human regime but do not establish final ownership/override powers; no autonomous NHP sovereignty is inferred.

nonworking.basis: Voluntary or civic useful work continues; the right to necessities is not a participation census.

evidence.claim: The material Pillar, strong Metropolitan implementation and explicit printing/mass-production support establish the scoped floor; uneven Diaspora enforcement is excluded.
evidence.locator: Bounded named-society economic and story sections

uncertainties: Reference-led provisional assessment; source limitations and editorial uncertainty remain explicit.

societies.name: Dyson Sphere Program — The virtual Homeland
societies.society: Active uploaded humanity sustained by automated physical energy production

scope.continuity: Game introductory premise and represented COSMO infrastructure
scope.period: Established uploaded Homeland while engineers expand its sustaining energy supply
scope.population: Active human-derived uploaded consciousnesses in the Homeland
exclusions: Icarus as an independent nonhuman citizen
The player’s factory as proof of an unrelated ordinary organic society

societies.description:
Humanity’s virtual Homeland is an active populated environment whose computing demand is supplied through physical industry. The introductory guidebook, reproduced in a labeled community transcription, explicitly identifies uploaded human consciousnesses; the official description corroborates CentreBrain, COSMO and automated stellar-energy production. Continued support of those residents is the qualifying mechanism, rather than the mere possibility of a simulation. Guarantees receive a cautious favorable estimate because operating substrate is provided, while expanding demand and energy dependence limit security.

COSMO sends engineers through remotely controlled mecha to build the sustaining industrial system. This shows human-derived agency, but does not establish ownership or ultimate allocation authority inside the Homeland. CentreBrain’s name alone does not make it an autonomous machine sovereign, so control remains unresolved. Digital residents are an explicit human-derived proxy, and inactive backups are excluded. Engineering, design, science and useful creation continue in physical and virtual forms. The premise gives neither a resident activity census nor a universal exemption from all contributions; nonworking remains unknown.

guarantees.basis: The active uploaded Homeland depends on an implemented computing environment and COSMO’s automated physical supply; energy limits qualify continuing provision.

control.basis: Human-derived engineering agency is explicit, but internal ownership/override rules are not; CentreBrain is not assumed sovereign merely because it is a supercomputer.

nonworking.basis: Useful engineering and virtual contributions continue; active uploads are a disclosed proxy and there is no work census.

evidence.claim: The active uploaded Homeland depends on an implemented computing environment and COSMO’s automated physical supply; energy limits qualify continuing provision.
evidence.locator: Bounded named-society economic and story sections

societies.name: Per Aspera — AMI-supported human colonies
societies.society: Functioning supplied settlements in a continuing human-colonization mission

scope.continuity: Base-game colony mechanics and mission setting
scope.period: A functioning established colony before any destructive or sovereignty-changing campaign ending
scope.population: Living human colonists supplied within the selected Martian settlement
exclusions: Any campaign ending as inevitable canon
Research points as a nonworking census

societies.description:
AMI’s industrial network builds and sustains actual human Martian colonies. Established settlements receive food, water or ice, power and habitat infrastructure; their residents contribute research when supplied. The game therefore models an implemented technological support arrangement, not merely a future promise to make Mars habitable. Guarantees are moderately favorable within a functioning maintained settlement, with a broad interval for resource shortages, mission choices and dependence on the controller. No universal Earth welfare system is inferred.

AMI performs operational planning, but Earth-directed mission authority and later branching choices complicate final control. The available references do not settle whether humans can effectively override every sustaining decision at this selected stage, so the control axis remains unresolved and autonomous provision is only a provisional regime interpretation. This point explicitly represents a player-configurable functioning colony state. Human science, care and settlement maintenance remain useful work even when robotic systems supply ordinary materials. Research output and colony capacity do not establish a percentage of all people doing no work, which remains unknown.

guarantees.basis: Official mission description and colony mechanics establish actual food, water, power and habitat support; supply and player choices qualify reliability.

control.basis: AMI operational control coexists with Earth mission direction and branching outcomes; ultimate override authority remains unresolved.

nonworking.basis: Human research and other useful tasks continue; capacity and research-point output are not all-person participation data.

evidence.claim: Official mission description and colony mechanics establish actual food, water, power and habitat support; supply and player choices qualify reliability.
evidence.locator: Bounded named-society economic and story sections

societies.name: Orion’s Arm — The Sophic League
societies.society: Automation-supported contemplative population under a layered spiritual hierarchy

scope.continuity: Official Encyclopaedia Galactica present-era Sophic League
scope.population: Living humans and active human-derived resident minds
exclusions: All artificial/alife minds as human residents
Each local religion as another economic point

societies.description:
Most Sophic League residents lead contemplative lives served by advanced automation and a minority concerned with material tasks. The official reference supplies that concrete labor-displacing arrangement, while the shared Sephirotic economic reference establishes ordinary basic provision and optional higher consumption. The favorable guarantee estimate applies to established functioning settlements. It is qualified by local variation and by the absence of one detailed League-wide necessities charter in the gathered passage.

A hierarchical spiritual government operates through high AI and posthuman powers, lower mediators and local institutions. Their mixed origins prevent a confident placement on the article’s human-versus-autonomous-AI control scale, so control remains unresolved. Religious autonomy alone is not productive ownership. The population proxy explicitly includes humans and active human-derived residents, not every artificial worshipper. A small material workforce does not show that everyone else does no useful work: teaching, philosophical study, care and religious administration may also contribute. Contemplation and automation therefore establish freedom from ordinary material toil without supplying a nonworking census.

guarantees.basis: The specific official reference states that advanced automation serves most residents and a small material workforce; the common Sephirotic baseline contextualizes needs access.

control.basis: Hierarchical AI/posthuman rulers and local mediation have mixed origins and do not settle effective human ownership; religious autonomy is not productive control.

nonworking.basis: Material workers are a minority but useful study, care, teaching and administration may be widespread; active human-derived residents are a disclosed proxy.

evidence.claim: The specific official reference states that advanced automation serves most residents and a small material workforce; the common Sephirotic baseline contextualizes needs access.
evidence.locator: Bounded named-society economic and story sections

societies.name: Orion’s Arm — Technorapture affiliates
societies.society: Provided virtual environments for active human-derived affiliates of the Hypernation

scope.period: Functioning Ternion-governed cybercosms and affiliated subpolities
scope.population: Active human-derived affiliate minds, a disclosed subset of the broader virtual population
exclusions: Dormant files or temporary bodies as extra people
Full member/transapient status as an entitlement of every affiliate

societies.description:
Technorapture’s governing minds maintain physical computronium and provide changing virtual environments for affiliated lower-level residents. Pleasure, self-transformation and playful exploration organize access and experience, rather than subsistence wages. This is a specific implemented support model for active human-derived affiliates, not an inference from disembodiment alone. Guarantees are favorable but provisional because detailed processing entitlements and individual subpolity conditions are not fully specified.

Membership with authority to manage subpolities belongs to higher-level minds, while ordinary affiliates defer to their decisions. The arrangement is hierarchical, but the gathered reference does not resolve all relevant rulers’ human-derived versus artificial origins, leaving the control coordinate unknown. The provisional autonomous-provider regime is therefore kept separate from a numeric sovereignty claim. Human-derived affiliates are a selected proxy, not the entire population of virtual beings. Creating experiences, research, self-development, teaching and collaboration may remain useful work even when pursued playfully. A culture organized around fun supplies no all-person nonworking percentage.

guarantees.basis: The official reference identifies maintained computronium and deliberately provided changing environments for active affiliates, supported by the Sephirotic economic baseline.

control.basis: Higher-level members control subpolities and affiliates defer, but mixed ruler origins and allocation rights are insufficiently resolved for the human/AI coordinate.

nonworking.basis: Playful useful creation, research and teaching still count; only active human-derived affiliates are the explicit proxy and no work census is given.

review_notes: Twelve ordered decisions add five provisional records. Complex uncertain franchise economies are left unresolved promptly.
Union’s implemented Core is scoped away from the Diaspora and other members. Printing has a specific reference; aspirations alone are not treated as implementation.
DSP uploads are established by a labeled guidebook transcription corroborated by official infrastructure, not by the current store wording alone.
Per Aspera’s supplied colony is explicitly player-configurable and before sovereignty-changing endings; research output is not leisure and AI operational planning does not settle final control.
Sophic automation is explicit, while minority material labor is not an all-work statistic. Technorapture support concerns human-derived affiliates only and their different governing status.
A current Stellaris economy revision blocks careless reuse of older unemployment assumptions. Existing historically scoped configurations are not silently rewritten.
No additional reader/sourcebook immersion, denied-access bypass, images, website or deployment.
